samira_lee: opened small PR to correct marlin-7b model card + catalog entry: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4812
samira_lee: TL;DR: clarify seq limit wording, add a tiny throughput row with GPU+batch metadata, swap SDK snippets to async v4, and call out CPU-quant fallback impact. quick eyes please before merge window.
jonathan_cho: skimmed. card shows seq_limit=12288 but bench CSV uses 6144. we should avoid implying validated 12k usage.
sophie_docs: Prefer exact language: "runtime technical max: 12288 (not validated for sustained throughput). Recommended prod ceiling: 6144 for latency-sensitive workloads." short and actionable.
jonathan_cho: add compatibility note: "KV cache grows O(seq_len) — enable prefix-caching for repeated contexts. Memory and tail latency increase with sequence length."
samira_lee: current snippet uses blocking client and max_tokens: ```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
resp = client.generate(model="marlin-7b", prompt="Translate...", max_tokens=64)
print(resp.text)
```
samira_lee: will replace with async streaming and max_new_tokens: ```python
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()
async with client.stream_generate(model="marlin-7b", prompt="Translate...", max_new_tokens=64) as s:
    async for chunk in s:
        print(chunk.text, end="")
```
sophie_docs: nice. add one-liner under limits: "If CPU fallback occurs for quantized variants, expect cold-start latency and ~2-4x throughput reduction".
bench-bot: linked bench CSV s3://redwood-bench/marlin-7b/2026-04-05.csv (ensure public path or GH asset mirror).
